title: Red Ryder
identity_notes: Juvenile Western adventure adapted from Fred Harman’s Red Ryder comic strip. Early stories used multi-part serial structure within a Tuesday/Thursday/Saturday schedule; later surviving programs are more episodic. The frozen GRH snapshot contains 65 playable/archive objects, including four without exact dates.

eras.label: Red Ryder radio run
eras.notes: NBC Blue launch followed by Mutual/Don Lee distribution; exact network-transition dates are not forced into the era record.

historical_context.title: Comic-strip Western adapted to juvenile radio
historical_context.description: Red Ryder moved from a highly popular newspaper comic-strip property into radio, preserving recurring characters while altering some story and character details for broadcasting.

historical_context.title: 1940s juvenile-Western representation of Native American characters
historical_context.description: Little Beaver was central to the radio property, but period dialogue and characterization used stereotyped conventions that are historically important to document rather than reproduce uncritically.

historical_context.title: Red Ryder Victory Patrol and wartime youth culture
historical_context.description: The radio program inspired the Red Ryder Victory Patrol, encouraging conservation and war-effort participation among young listeners.

historical_context.title: Sponsor-supported juvenile adventure radio
historical_context.description: Langendorf Bread sponsorship, premiums and decoder-style audience participation tied the adventure serial to children’s commercial radio culture.
